summary: Sustained elevated 5xx rate after runtime-proxy CPU-throttle causing accept-queue backlog
description:
Issue summary:
We observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for a small set of Nimbus Health requests beginning 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC. Errors persisted for ~2 hours with intermittent partial recovery, correlated with high CPU steal/limits on the runtime-proxy layer.

Impact:
- Customer: Nimbus Health (dedicated) reported ~18% failed requests for generation endpoints (chat and streaming sessions) for ~2 hours.
- User-visible failures: 503 and 502 responses, streaming disconnects mid-response, and increased tail latency (p95 -> p99).
- Business impact: Production traffic degraded; customer reported active user sessions failing and triggering client-side retries.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east, dedicated tenant pool for Nimbus Health
- Components implicated: runtime-proxy (sidecar handling keepalive and connection multiplexing), upstream serving runtime (model shards), and API gateway fronting tenant routes
- Recent changes: Autoscaler firmware update (2026-03-09), kernel security backport applied to several host images (2026-03-08)

Observed behavior / Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a sustained small-batch streaming session from customer tenant (~10 rps across long-lived streams).
2) After ~5-10 minutes, accept-queue for proxy climbs and requests start returning 502/503.
3) Some worker processes show high user CPU waits and occasional preemption logs.

Logs & metrics snapshot (references):
- Grafana: dashboard panel "tenant/nimbus/5xx-rate" spike at 09:20 UTC (link in related_confluence_pages)
- Host metrics: runtime-proxy CPU steal and system load elevated on hosts hst-us-east-27/28
- Proxy logs: repeated "accept queue full" WARN messages and "connection reset by peer" entries (sample log IDs: log://prod/us-east/hst-us-east-27/2026-03-10/09:23/az4)
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 09:18 UTC: first 502 observed by customer.
- 09:20 UTC: platform alert (5xx rate > 8% for tenant) triggered.
- 09:22 UTC: SRE pulled metrics; host CPU shows long-running kernel scheduling stalls on runtime-proxy.
- 09:25 UTC: small-scale remedial action: moved two proxy instances to different hosts; partial reduction in p95 but 5xx persisted.

Hypotheses considered:
- a) Kernel-level CPU throttling or noisy neighbor on hosts causing proxy accept-queue to fill.
- b) Runtime-proxy CPU limit misconfiguration combined with recent autoscaler behavior causing too many concurrent prefetched streams.
- c) A regression in the proxy connection handling path leading to a tight accept-loop under high keepalive counts.

Evidence pointing to (a) and (b):
- Host-level metrics show CPU steal and cgroup throttling events correlated with error spikes.
- Autoscaler activity logs show a brief oscillation (scale-up then scale-down) around 09:10-09:17 UTC after which tenant request patterns concentrated on a subset of hosts.
- No recent code change in proxy binaries between 2026-03-01 and incident window per PR history (related_github_prs).

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Evacuated two runtime-proxy pods from hst-us-east-27 and hst-us-east-28 at 09:25 UTC to reduce local contention.
- Increased proxy accept-queue size on the tenant route for 30 minutes (09:30-10:00 UTC) as an emergency measure.
- Engaged autoscaler to temporarily hold minimal scale-downs for the tenant pool.

Data collected and attached:
- Host system traces (perf samples) from hst-us-east-27 and 28 (internal trace IDs added to confluence page).
- Request samples with headers and small stack traces attached to ticket comment 2.
- API gateway traces showing retry amplification patterns for the tenant.
next_steps:
Short term:
- Keep autoscaler scale-downs paused for Nimbus tenant for 24 hours and monitor 5xx rate.
- Proactively shift tenant proxy instances across hosts to reduce contention.
- Add temporary rate-limiter on long-lived streaming connections for this tenant to prevent accept-queue saturation.

Mid term:
- Reproduce CPU throttle pattern in staging with synthetic long-lived streams and autoscaler oscillation to validate fixes.
- Tune proxy cgroup CPU shares and accept-queue defaults for high-keepalive tenants.
- Adjust autoscaler hysteresis to avoid rapid scale down after short-lived spikes.

Long term:
- Kernel upgrade assessment to eliminate host-level scheduling stalls.
- Implement more granular tenant placement logic to prevent host concentration.

Owners:
- SRE lead: Ravi Patel
- Runtime/Proxy eng: Maria Gomez
- Customer success: Jordan Lee
workaround: Applied: host-level rebalancing and proxy accept-queue increase; paused scale-downs. Customer advised to reduce parallel long-lived streams temporarily. These measures reduced 5xx rate to ~2% by 10:45 UTC.

2026-03-10 09:50 - Maria Gomez (Runtime): Confirmed no proxy binary changes in window. Request samples show clustered connections with long-lived keepalives. Investigating cgroup settings.

2026-03-11 14:05 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Completed staging repro plan and started synthetic test runs. Initial results show similar accept-queue growth when autoscaler oscillates rapidly under this workload pattern.

resolution: In progress - mitigation reduced error rate to acceptable levels for customer. Scheduled a controlled rollout of proxy cgroup CPU share increase and autoscaler hysteresis tuning (planned 2026-03-15). Post-implementation monitoring and a follow-up technical postmortem will be completed by 2026-03-20.
